previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, failed renal and pancreas transplants, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and autonomic neuropathy was admitted due to elevated INR over 9 and pink dialysate, concerning for bleeding. She also presented with hypoglycemia-related altered mental status, pleuritic chest pain, and poor oral intake. Vitamin K was given for the coagulopathy, warfarin was held and later restarted at 1 mg daily as the INR normalized. The pink dialysate resolved. A CT chest showed bilateral pleural effusions and a right apical opacity, but no signs of active infection; antibiotics were not needed. Tacrolimus was reduced due to a high level. Malnutrition was addressed with nutritional support. She remained stable, was discharged to extended care, and will follow up with her transplant, nephrology, and cardiology teams.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  CHF, lethargy and hypotension.  Please assess for pneumonia or
pulmonary edema.

TECHNIQUE:  AP upright portable chest radiograph.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:

Bilateral moderate size pleural effusions are increased with increased
interstitial markings and vascular congestion compatible with moderate to
severe pulmonary edema.  Mid and lower lung right greater than left pulmonary
opacities, may reflect atelectasis in this setting of effusions and pulmonary
edema, however a in multifocal infectious process or aspiration cannot be
excluded.  Moderate cardiomegaly persists unchanged.  Patient is status post
median sternotomy and cardiac valve replacement.

IMPRESSION:

Moderate to severe congestive failure with bilateral moderate-sized pleural
effusions, increased.  As these findings could mask an underlying infectious
process, if clinical concern persists repeat imaging after diuresis is
recommended.
